description: The course offers a geographical approach for understanding human-environment interactions on the Earth. This hands-on course examines the ecosystem services framework for identifying, interpreting (description-based) and integrating data for Environmental Analysis. Lab exercises provide opportunities to develop applied skills in the use of quantitative and qualitative variables and methods. Ethical values are emphasized for assessing challenges and opportunities to increase stakeholder participation towards environmental justice at different scales (local, state, national, regional). Methods and techniques in science are vast and impossible to be thoroughly covered in one single course, however, this holistic approach is wide-ranging and relates the use of theories, ArcGIS Pro software, creation of databases and maps. Students will explore various topics through practical exercises using principles on geomorphology, hydrology, geology, soils, climate, vegetation, land use/cover, population distribution, population occupation, spatial pattern analysis and survey design. Prerequisite: ENVST 137.
